judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four specific institutional categories are followed by two open catch-alls (any Person approved by Administrative Borrower, or by Lender during an Event of Default), which largely swallows the enumerated criteria.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 14.1(a) then says the Assignee "need not be an Eligible Transferee" in a merger or portfolio sale, so the definition's limits are already qualified elsewhere; the two fit together but loosely.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long list of communication types ending in "or other communication" from any Governmental Authority "or any third party" — a very wide catch-all against enumerated specifics.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It supports Sections 6.13(d) and 11.3(c) and the Environmental Liabilities and Costs definition; no contradiction found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[B]inding and enforceable guideline, binding and enforceable written policy, or rule of common law" plus a long "including" statute list leaves the outer boundary of the term contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.14 and 6.13 and the Environmental Lien definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sweeping damages language ("punitive damages, consequential damages, treble damages") but each head is enumerated and tied to an Environmental Action.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits Section 11.3(c)'s indemnity and the Environmental Lien definition; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short definition built on two other defined terms; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 6.13(a) and (d)(i).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Incorporates the Code term and adds an inclusive list with express exclusions; well bounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Borrower Collateral clause (e), Section 5.4 and Permitted Dispositions clause (a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory reference; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in the Benefit Plan and ERISA Affiliate definitions and Section 5.13.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Technical, entirely keyed to specific IRC sections with express purpose limitations.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Supports Section 5.13's representation; no inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.6(e) does create the Escrow Account, and Borrower Collateral clause (d) expressly includes Escrow Accounts; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference to a whole Section.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8 does define the term, although its subsections are numbered erratically (8.4-8.6 appear as 3.4-3.6); that is a typographic rather than substantive problem.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory reference; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in the Stock definition; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A bare list of five individuals, with no office or role attached to any of them.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.13 makes it a default if an Executive Officer ceases "to be employed in his current position with Manager or Servicer", yet the definition identifies no positions — a real gap between definition and operative clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Descriptive definition of a document; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1(a) requires delivery of exactly this letter; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Trivial cross-reference to the preamble.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble does designate R.E. Loans, LLC as "Fund"; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-line definition; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(a)-(b) use Funding Date the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard accounting definition; "consistently applied" and "as in effect from time to time" are in mild tension but conventionally so.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 1.2 and Section 7.11 (which permits changes required to conform to GAAP) work with it; no conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An extremely long inclusive list closed by a residual "any other personal property other than" five excluded categories, so the boundary is actually drawn by the exclusions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Coheres with the Borrower Collateral clause (f) and Sections 4.3 and 4.5(f).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enumerated documents followed by "or other organizational documents" — a modest catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3.1(d), 5.9(b)(i), 7.3(a) and 7.10(a)(ii) all use the term consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Enumerated bodies followed by "or other similar dispute-resolving panel or body"; the inclusion of arbitration panels within "Governmental Authority" is odd but express.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used consistently in Sections 3.1(q), 5.9, 6.10 and 8.16.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is circular with "Guaranty", which is itself defined by reference to a Guarantor.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No guaranty is required by Section 3.1 and no Guarantor is a party, yet Sections 9.1(f), 16.7 and the Lender Expenses definition all refer to Guarantors; the term floats without an operative anchor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Guaranty means any Guaranty executed and delivered by a Guarantor" defines the term by itself — a genuine circularity.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Paired with the Guarantor definition the circle closes with no external content, and nothing in the operative text requires a guaranty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clause (a) ends in "any other formulation intended to define, list, or classify substances by reason of deleterious properties", a broad general phrase against specific listed categories.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 5.14, 6.13 and 11.3(c).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A list of derivative types closed by "or similar transactions" and limited by a stated hedging purpose; the purpose qualifier could be argued about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Bank Product clause (g) and Indebtedness clause (f) both reference Hedge Agreements consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Seven enumerated categories with express carve-outs; broad but tightly drawn, and clause (g) is limited to the preceding clauses.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.1 lists the permitted exceptions and Section 5.20 the scheduled Indebtedness; the scheme is coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 11.3 does define the term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 11.3 does define the term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[F]ormal or informal moratoria, compositions, extensions generally with creditors" is loose, and "commenced by or against any Person" sweeps in third parties.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 8.4 and 8.5 distinguish voluntary from involuntary proceedings and give the involuntary case a 45-day cure, which this definition does not itself reflect; the two read together sensibly enough.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defers to GAAP treatment; determinate for accounting purposes.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Feeds the Tangible Net Worth definition and Section 7.16(a); consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed calendar-month period; unusually simple and therefore determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.12(b) requires election three Business Days before the period commences and Section 2.12(c) deems election absent notice; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Incorporates the Code term; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Permitted Dispositions clause (b) and Borrower Collateral clause (g) use it; a mortgage fund holding inventory is unlikely but harmless.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Broad but enumerated, with express exclusions and a GAAP backstop.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.12 permits only Permitted Investments, and clause (d) of that definition covers the Borrowers' core lending business; coherent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Incorporates the Code term; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Borrower Collateral clause (h) and Section 4.7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]n interest in a member's interest in Fund" is a doubled and awkward formulation whose scope (the membership interest itself, or a derivative interest in it) is not obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 5.20, 7.10 and 8.9(x) all turn on Investor Membership Interests and the Permitted Reorganization exchanges them for Approved Debt, so the imprecision matters across the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory reference; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in the ERISA Affiliate definition; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Trivial cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble names Wells Fargo Foothill, LLC as Lender.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A ten-clause catalogue with internal qualifiers such as "up to the amount of any limitation contained in this Agreement", which requires cross-hunting to apply, and clause (j) is very broad.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.1(e) and (o) charge amounts as "Lender Group Expenses", a term nowhere defined in this bilateral agreement, so the expense scheme does not fully line up.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short enumerated definition; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used in Section 11.3 and Section 16.11's indemnity; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Schedule cross-reference only.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 2.3(a), 2.6 and 2.7 use Lender's Account consistently.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 4.1, 5.9(e), 8.14 and 3.6's release mechanics.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.12(b) defines the LIBOR Deadline as stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Form cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit L-1 is referenced but the executed copy attaches only Exhibits B-1, B-2 and C-1; a missing-exhibit gap rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.12(a) defines the LIBOR Option as stated.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise formula with a stated rounding convention and adjustment trigger.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Base LIBOR Rate, Reserve Percentage definitions and Section 2.12.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Definitional and mechanical.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Matches Section 2.12(a) and the Applicable Margin definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Extraordinarily broad — it sweeps in easements, covenants, leases and "other title exceptions" as "Liens", which strains the ordinary meaning of the word.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.2 forbids suffering any Lien except Permitted Liens, and Permitted Liens clause (k) rescues only non-interfering easements on Real Property, so ordinary title exceptions on Note Receivable Collateral sit awkwardly in the scheme.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.9 does create the Loan Account.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Named documents followed by "any other agreement entered into, now or in the future, by any Borrower and Lender in connection with this Agreement" — an unbounded catch-all against a specific list.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Bank Product Agreements are Loan Documents here but are carved out of Section 15.1's amendment rule, and the Servicing Agreement is a Loan Document although Section 8.15 treats breach of it separately; workable but with seams.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Trivial cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The preamble designates B-4 Partners LLC as Manager; consistent with Section 16.11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A textbook material-adverse-change clause: "material adverse change in the business, prospects, operations ... taken as a whole" is the paradigm of a vague standard courts are asked to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is used as a condition in Section 3.3(d) and as a qualifier in Sections 5.10, 6.10, 8.9 and 3.1(f) consistently; the difficulty is intrinsic rather than relational.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference; determinate on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The agreement contains two provisions numbered 3.4 ("Term" and "Intentionally Blank"), so the cross-reference points into a mis-numbered sequence, though the intended target is obvious.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single dollar figure; nothing whatever to construe in the words.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.16(b) caps the Senior Leverage Ratio (Obligations divided by Tangible Net Worth) at 0.9%, which against the $600,000,000 minimum Tangible Net Worth would permit only about $5.4 million of Obligations — irreconcilable with a $50,000,000 revolver.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A defined eleven-month period stated by reference to the Closing Date; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 2.10(c) and 2.10(e) both key the $20,000,000 minimum to this period consistently.
